body:
## Finding

`fleet-paperwork create`'s readback verification checks only the created issue's title and number — not the body, state, or labels — although the tool's README promises the readback compares "(title, body, state)". A create whose body was dropped or mangled, or whose labels were not applied, passes as "created+verified".

## Evidence

- Source PR: #3692 (merged, merge `ad1b664351d543575828b2d49ed0800fb30432a9`, head `240bab31582b8851ef2717abcd157089ce42a752`).
- `infra/fleet-paperwork/README.md` on current main (`4cd2927643453bee47a0f764de534e229220cf88`): "A filing is verified, or it is a failure. Every create / comment / close is followed by a readback GET, and the result is compared (title, body, state…)".
- `infra/fleet-paperwork/fleet_paperwork.py` on current main (same commit, verified twice): `cmd_create` at line 337; its readback is `if got.get("title") != title or got.get("number") != number: die(...)` — body, state, and the labels sent in the payload are never compared. (`cmd_comment` does compare the comment body; create is the odd one out.)

## Why it matters

The tool's whole contract — relied on by the rate-limit outbox workflow — is that a reported success means the filing is actually there, complete. An issue created with an empty/mangled body carries none of the evidence or acceptance criteria the filer sent, yet every downstream consumer (queue packets, backlog entries, dedupe) treats the create as verified.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Create readback compares at least body and state (and labels when labels were requested) against what was sent, dying on mismatch like the title check does.
- [ ] A unit test with a readback payload whose body differs proves the failure; a matching payload passes.
- [ ] Existing fleet-paperwork tests still pass.
